newsitem.title: USA: Japan may delay expansion of insurance subsidiaries.
newsitem.headline: Japan may delay expansion of insurance subsidiaries.

text.p: Finance Minister Wataru Kubo and U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky met on Sunday to discuss a simmering dispute on insurance trade, but remain far apart on the issues, a senior official from Japan's Ministry of Finance said.
Kubo and Barshefsky met over dinner and exchanged views on how to proceed with bilateral insurance talks, but did not set a date for the next meeting, the official said.
He said Sunday's meeting was not a place for negotiations, so the two countries remained far apart on a dispute over U.S. allegations that Tokyo is poised to renege on a 1994 insurance trade pact.
Japan told the United States that it may delay the entry of Japanese insurance subsidiaries into the so-called third sector niche market until Jan. 1, the official said.
He added that the conditions for operating in the third sector market will be presented to the insurance subsidiaries on Sept. 30 as planned.

The official was asked whether Japan had told the United States that it may delay Japanese insurance subsidiaries' entry into some products in the so-called third sector market, which covers accident policies and coverage for some diseases.
He said Kubo had discussed the matter with U.S. Ambassador to Japan Walter Mondale and Barshefsky before Sunday's meeting.
Kubo is in Washington to attend the regular meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, as well as the Group of Seven industrialised nations.
The U.S. side did not mention any threat of sanctions during Sunday's talks, the official said.
Talks between Kubo and Barshefsky were followed by discussions on an administrative level.
